Package edu.cnu.mdi.item

Interface ITextEditable

All Known Implementing Classes:
MapTextItem, TextItem
public interface ITextEditable
Marks an item as having editable text content, font, and style — the minimal contract required by TextEditDialog.

Purpose

TextEditDialog was originally written to accept a concrete TextItem. Introducing this interface breaks that dependency so the dialog can operate on any text-bearing item — in particular both TextItem (world-space anchor) and MapTextItem (geographic anchor) — without knowing about either class.

Implementing classes

Any item that can be edited by TextEditDialog should implement this interface. Typically that means declaring implements ITextEditable on the class; the six methods are usually already present.

Method contract

  • getText() / setText(String) — the full text content as a single string with embedded newlines for multi-line text.
  • getFont() / setFont(Font) — the display font. Passing null to setFont should restore a sensible default.
  • getStyle() / setStyle(IStyled) — the fill, line, and text colors (and any other style attributes) for this item.

  • Method Details

    • getText

      String getText()
      Returns the current text content.

      Multi-line text is represented with embedded '\n' characters. Implementations must never return null; an empty string is the correct representation of no content.

      Returns:
      the text; never null

    • setText

      void setText(String text)
      Replaces the text content.
      Parameters:
      text - the new text; implementations should treat null as an empty string

    • getFont

      Font getFont()
      Returns the current display font.
      Returns:
      the font; must not be null in a correctly initialised item

    • setFont

      void setFont(Font font)
      Sets the display font.
      Parameters:
      font - the new font; passing null should restore the implementation's default font

    • getStyle

      IStyled getStyle()
      Returns the current style (colors, line style, etc.).
      Returns:
      the style; may be null on a partially constructed or disposed item, but must not be null during normal use

    • setStyle

      void setStyle(IStyled style)
      Replaces the current style.
      Parameters:
      style - the new style; null is accepted but may cause rendering errors unless getStyleSafe() is used subsequently
